text:
joel: heads-up: during the 11:00 attach wave in us-west3-d we're seeing a spike of ContainerCreating delays (~20-45s). several batch pods timed out. nvme util on affected hosts is >95% during the window. looks like janitor scrub overlap with autoscaler launches.

anya: can you paste the node logs you saw? small snippets ok.

joel: pasted quick samples from one host: 

# iostat -x 1 2
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await  %util
nvme0n1         1100.0  3000.0  48000  405000     128.0     2.6   9.6   96.8

[ 7890.100000] scrubber[2210]: async scrub starting on nvme0n1 cohort=us-west3-d-3
[ 7890.102000] nvme0n1: queue depth saturated, fallback throttle
[ 7890.350000] kubelet: attach timeout waiting for ephemeral disk

kubectl describe pod batch-run-zzz
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Warning AttachError  1m   kubelet            Attach timed out: iops spike on /var/lib/kubelet/plugins\npatrick: this matches the scrub-scheduler change we shipped last week (dynamic per-host windows). dynamic windows improved daytime latency overall, but it can line up badly for bulk attaches.

anya: short-term fixes we can try now?

patrick: options: 1) label a small cohort and pause scrub for the next 30-60m; 2) reduce scrub process ioprio so it yields to attach; 3) set a scheduler hint so autoscaler prefers nodes labelled ephemeral-quiet=true during the attach wave.

joel: i'm going to pause scrub on cohort us-west3-d-3 and lower scrub ioprio to 6. i'll also apply ephemeral-quiet label as a hint.

sre-bot: [action] label infra.janitor.pause=true applied to cohort us-west3-d-3 at 1729801230

sre-bot: [action] scrub process ioprio set to 6 on hosts in cohort us-west3-d-3 at 1729801232

sre-bot: [info] scheduler hint prefer_ephemeral_quiet=true set for upcoming autoscaler attaches in cohort us-west3-d-3

anya: any quick metric delta after changes?

joel: attach success went from ~69% -> 95% in the first 3m after changes. nvme util dropped from ~97% -> ~60% within ~90s on the most impacted hosts.

patrick: nice. follow-ups: 1) collect nvme smart logs and firmware versions for 6 impacted hosts and open ticket if util remains high; 2) RFC to integrate scrub-scheduler with autoscaler forecasts so scrub can back off proactively; 3) consider automatic ioprio lowering when attach waves are predicted.

hw-team: if util stays >90% after mitigations, we'll need to check thermal events and SMART counters for wear; please gather `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1` and `nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvme0n1`.

joel: creating ticket TICKET-4982 with logs and smart dumps. leaving the pause label for 45m while backlog drains, then we'll gradually resume scrub with staggered windows.

anya: cost note - pausing scrubs adds backlog which increases total scrub IO hours (~+3-7% over 24h depending on backlog), and slightly more wear spread. but it prevents attach timeouts that waste GPU time and increase customer latency. math suggests it's net-positive for heavy attach waves. we'll include precise numbers in the RFC.

patrick: thanks. i'll draft the RFC for scrub/autoscaler tie-in and ping sched-team + infra-ops. update thread with postmortem if this repeats. :thumbsup:
